brief.headline: Close a ₹16.09 L/year price gap to Mars Plastics on bottles and caps, and cut payment days to free up ₹10.63 L cash.

priceAsk.summary: Match Mars Plastics on the 30 ml bottle (₹1.38/NOS) and the 28 mm cap (₹0.81/NOS); bring all items down to what Mars charges us.
priceAsk.basis: We already buy the same bottles and caps from Mars Plastics at ₹1.38/NOS and ₹0.81/NOS — Premier charges ₹1.65/NOS and ₹0.90/NOS for identical items. Mars proves these prices work. The open market for the 28 mm cap sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical (market-fair verdict), so ₹0.81/NOS is within reach.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹10.63 L cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic is private and publishes no financials, so we cannot see their revenue, profit or how tight cash is for them. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend is the only scale marker we have. Without their numbers, the plan leans on our own purchase data — we know Mars gives us better prices on the same items — and on lining up a strong second source so we are not stuck. Because we can't gauge their health, we push firmly on price (the gap is clear) but stay ready to walk if they won't move.

evidence.point: We pay Premier ₹1.65/NOS for the 30 ml HDPE bottle; Mars Plastics charges us ₹1.38/NOS for the same item.
We pay Premier ₹0.90/NOS for the 28 mm PP cap with induction wad; Mars Plastics charges us ₹0.81/NOS.
Closing these gaps on just two items saves us ₹15.97 L a year; total excess across all items is ₹16.09 L.
The open market for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap runs ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, so Mars's ₹0.81/NOS is achievable and Premier's ₹0.90/NOS sits near the high end.
Moving payment from 45 days to 30 days frees up ₹10.63 L cash for us; a further 15-day cut (to 15 days) would free another ₹5.31 L.
evidence.figure: ₹10.63 L at 30 days, ₹5.31 L more at 15 days

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — a top second-source candidate with proven scale and solid health.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong, profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Manufacturer, India-Pan presence — a very strong backup lead if we need resin-to-bottle integration, but requires qualification.

risks: Premier publishes no financials, so we fly blind on their revenue, profit and cash position — we cannot tell if a hard push will tip them or if they can afford to match Mars.
We spend ₹1.29 Cr a year with them; without their revenue figure we don't know if that buys us real leverage or if we are a small account they can afford to lose.
Mars Plastics already supplies us at lower prices, so if Premier won't move we can shift more volume to Mars — but check Mars's capacity before leaning too hard on this threat.

The 28 mm cap market is ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical (market-fair verdict), so there is modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — but ₹0.81/NOS may be close to floor for the current spec and quantity.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We've been paying you ₹1.65 for the 30 ml bottle and ₹0.90 for the 28 mm cap, but Mars Plastics gives us ₹1.38 and ₹0.81 on identical items — help us understand why we should keep the premium with you.
